To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) TransferTransfo trained with written data is very vulnerable to ASR errors in the dialog history and (2) introducing ASR hypotheses during training is a promising baseline mitigation strategy.

(a) TransferTransfo, an end-to-end open domain chatbot trained on written data, is very sensitive to ASR hypotheses introduced to the dialogue history at test time; (b) as a baseline mitigation strategy we introduce synthetic ASRs to the dialog history at training time, but observe marginal improvements; (c) we hope this work will encourage the community to consider speech robustness as a key evaluation criterion in open-domain dialog research.
